questions.explain: RDS storage billing has four categories: provisioned volume (gp2 $0.115 / gp3 $0.092 per GB-month), automated backups (free up to 100% of provisioned storage, then $0.095/GB-month), manual snapshots ($0.095/GB-month from creation, never auto-expire), and cross-region copies (egress + destination storage). Typical distribution: forgotten manual snapshots are 20–35% of the storage bill — the first target.
options: Only the provisioned volume is billed
Snapshots are free; only backup retention is billed

Provisioned volume, automated backups (free up to 100% of provisioned storage), manual snapshots (never expire automatically), and cross-region copies — with forgotten manual snapshots typically 20–35% of the bill
Storage billing is a flat fee per instance

questions.explain: The tagging convention requires RetentionDays (30/90/365 or `permanent`), CreatedBy, and Purpose on every manual snapshot; `permanent` is exempt, everything else gets evaluated by a daily scheduled Lambda that deletes past-retention snapshots. Untagged snapshots older than MAX_AGE_DAYS (default 90) get deleted; run with DRY_RUN=true the first week before going live.
options: No tagging is needed; delete all snapshots older than 7 days

Tag every manual snapshot with RetentionDays/CreatedBy/Purpose; a daily Lambda deletes expired-retention snapshots (permanent exempt, untagged older than the hard cap deleted); run DRY_RUN for the first week
Snapshots expire automatically after 30 days
Only delete snapshots manually in the console

questions.explain: Measure avg_fragmentation_in_percent from sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats (leaf level): ≥30% → REBUILD (ONLINE=ON on Enterprise/Azure SQL), 10–30% → REORGANIZE, below 10% → monitor — an index at 80% fragmentation is ~5x the storage its data needs. On vCore Azure SQL the benefit is mainly performance unless you then reduce provisioned max storage.
options: Fragmentation ≥30% → REBUILD, 10–30% → REORGANIZE, <10% → monitor, measured via avg_fragmentation_in_percent; 80% fragmentation means ~5x over-allocation
Rebuild all indexes nightly regardless of fragmentation
Fragmentation never affects storage costs
Only reorganize; never rebuild
questions.q: How is index fragmentation diagnosed and what thresholds drive REBUILD vs REORGANIZE?

questions.explain: On RDS SQL Server, tempdb lives on a separate unbilled NVMe SSD — it's an instance-size concern: excessive tempdb causes PAGELATCH allocation contention that can force an upsize; fix it by replacing #temp tables with @table variables for small sets or using TRUNCATE instead of DROP/CREATE in loops. For log bloat, check log_reuse_wait_desc: LOG_BACKUP means increase log backup frequency (e.g., every 15 min vs 60), ACTIVE_TRANSACTION means a long-running transaction is blocking truncation.
options: Tempdb is billed per GB; log files shrink automatically
Ignore tempdb and transaction logs
Only shrink the log file weekly

Tempdb on RDS is unbilled (separate NVMe) but causes PAGELATCH contention — prefer table variables for small sets and TRUNCATE-in-loop over DROP/CREATE; for log bloat check log_reuse_wait_desc: LOG_BACKUP → more frequent log backups, ACTIVE_TRANSACTION → find the blocking transaction
